title: Availability sets, availability zones and what each one protects against

videos.script: Something in a datacentre fails every day: a disk, a host, a power supply, and once in a long while a whole building. {{scale}} This lesson is about which of those failures the shop's machines survive. What decides it is where the copies are, not how many there are. {{set}} An availability set spreads machines across racks. A rack that loses power takes one row of them, and a maintenance reboot takes one column. You will write a set in Bicep and compile it on your laptop. {{zones}} Availability zones go further, and put machines in separate buildings of the same region. You will place two machines in two zones, with one address for both, and see two mistakes the compiler lets through. {{sla}} Then the arithmetic. Microsoft promises a percentage, and a percentage is minutes: ninety-nine point nine is forty-three minutes in thirty days. A short Python program multiplies the parts of a chain, and combines copies that stand in for each other. {{neither}} Last, what none of it protects against. A region, a bad release, a bug in your own code. Every copy shares those.
